extra.message: The id query parameter from req.query['id'] is concatenated directly into the shell command passed to child_process.exec('ping ' + id). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; rm -rf /', '&& whoami') to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

User-controlled query parameters id and id2 are concatenated and passed directly to eval(id + id2). This allows arbitrary server-side JavaScript execution (RCE), e.g. id=require('child_process').execSync('id')&id2=.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: The login handler builds the MongoDB query from request body values without type validation. When req.body.password contains '{' it is passed through JSON.parse and stored as an object, so an attacker can supply operators such as {"$ne":""} (or an email containing '{' via body-parser extended mode) and authenticate as any user without knowing the password.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The /getdata route does JSON.parse(req.query['id']) and passes the resulting value straight into the MongoDB query find({ id: id }). Supplying a JSON object with query operators (e.g. id={"$gt":0} or id={"$ne":null}) injects MongoDB operators and can return arbitrary user records.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The /a6_misconfig route parses the attacker-controlled accountno field with JSON.parse and uses it directly as the MongoDB query find({ accountno: accno }). A JSON object containing operators such as {"$ne":null} or {"$gt":""} allows NoSQL operator injection to dump records.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The /insecure_deserialization route serializes a user-influenced object with node-serialize and immediately calls serialize.unserialize() on the resulting string. node-serialize.unserialize evaluates values containing the _$$ND_FUNC$$_ marker, so deserializing attacker-influenced data is a known remote code execution sink.

The server's /xss_r response echoes the unencoded id parameter (index.js:170) and the client wraps it with $sce.trustAsHtml, then renders it via ng-bind-html in a7_xss_reflected.html:34. This disables Angular's contextual escaping and yields DOM/reflected XSS when id contains HTML such as .

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /xss_r handler reflects the raw user-supplied id query parameter back to the caller in res.json({cmd: result, search: id}). The response is consumed by the client which renders search through $sce.trustAsHtml/ng-bind-html, resulting in reflected XSS.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /insecure_dor endpoint returns account records based solely on the attacker-supplied accountno with no authentication or ownership check. Any caller can enumerate account numbers and read other users' bank/account data (IDOR / broken object level authorization).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The /a3sensitive endpoint looks up users by a user-supplied id and returns the entire document with no projection or authorization. This leaks sensitive fields including the plaintext password stored in the users collection.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The /a3sensitive_header endpoint serializes and returns the caller's complete request headers (JSON.stringify(req.headers)) including Cookie, Authorization and other sensitive values, causing information disclosure.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Authentication is implemented only in the /service_login handler, which is never registered as middleware (app.use('/service_login', ...)); it is merely a route. As a result every sensitive API (e.g. /getdata, /a3sensitive, /ping, /eval, /insecure_dor, /a6_misconfig, /insecure_deserialization) is reachable without any session check, allowing unauthenticated access.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The express-session secret is hardcoded as the static value "Your secret key". A predictable session signing key lets an attacker forge/tamper session cookies and hijack authenticated sessions.

cwe: CWE-547: Use of Hard-coded, Security-relevant Constants

extra.message: In /a6_misconfig the raw database/driver error object is returned to the client via res.json(err) (see also line 188). This exposes internal implementation details, connection information and stack data that aid further attacks.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
